learning_outcomes.text: Performing operating activities, maintenance, service, integration of industrial robot systems.
Identification of roles and responsibilities in a multi-specialized team, making decisions and assigning tasks, applying techniques of effective relationships and team working.

Familiarization with the basic theoretical and practical knowledge about the use of industrial robots. This knowledge can be a real help for graduates from the specialization Electromechanics, to their integration into industrial production systems with robots.
Present theoretical elements related to the structure, basic kinematic models, programming and integration of industrial robots into Cells/Manufacturing systems.
Familiarize students with practical aspects of programming industrial robots for automation parts handling operations in cells/manufacturing systems.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION TO INDUSTRIAL ROBOTS.
THE MECHANICAL SYSTEM OF AN INDUSTRIAL ROBOT.
THE DRIVE SYSTEM OF AN INDUSTRIAL ROBOT.
THE CONTROL SYSTEM OF AN INDUSTRIAL ROBOT.
THE GEOMETRIC MODEL OF AN INDUSTRIAL ROBOT.
PROGRAMMING OF INDUSTRIAL ROBOTS.
Definitions. Robot applications. The block scheme of an industrial robot.
The general structure of the mechanical system of a serial robot. The structure of the kinematic joints.
Block structure of the mechanical system. The structure of the trajectory generating mechanism (MGT). Structure of the orientation mechanism.
Characteristic point, characteristic line and auxiliary line. Tool Center Point (TCP). The structure of the mechanical system of a parallel robot.
The general block scheme of the drive system. Electric drive system.
Hydraulic drive system. Pneumatic drive system.
Control system. General structure of the control system, Case studies.
Control methods of an industrial robot. Sequential control. Point to Point control (PTP). Multipoint control (MTP). Control on continuous path CP (Continuous Path).
Defining the geometric model of an industrial robot. Settings the coordinate systems. Example for a robot type TRT.
Calculation of homogeneous transformation matrices. Calculation example for a TRT robot.
Getting of the direct geometric model and the inverse geometric model.
Programming of industrial robots. Online and offline programming methods.
Examples of programming languages for industrial robots. MRL programming language – Mitsubishi Robot Language. Apps.
Kuka KRL programming language. Positioning and motion control commands. Digital input/output controls. Commands for program control.
Presentation of the laboratory and the labor protection norms.
Programming the RV-M1 robot to perform a handling operation.
Programming the movement of the RV-M1 robot on Slide.
Programming the RV-M1 robot for the service of VISION 2000 station.
Programming the RV-M1 robot to perform an assembly operation.
Control a mobile robot equipped with Arduino Mega development system.
Closing the situation at the laboratory.
teaching_methods: Presentation of the course with video projector
Laboratory work within an educational CIM system
assessment_rules: For the course, a minimum mark of 5 is required, which implies knowledge of fundamental notions without presenting details. For a grade of 10, thorough knowledge of all subjects is required. For the laboratory, a minimum grade of 5 is required, necessitating recognition of the tools used in laboratory works. Students receive a test and grade at each laboratory, and also a grade for the laboratory work during the semester and for the laboratory work file, resulting in an average for the laboratory.
